canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.statement: The SERVER implements report immutability in full: revisions are retained, marked superseded, linked to their successor, and remain byte-identical and downloadable. §285 measured all of it. The CLIENT calls none of it — only GET /inspection-reports and GET /inspection-reports/:id/download. It never calls /revisions and never calls /versions/:version/download.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.measured: Reopen -> material change -> re-complete -> regenerate. Revision 1 retained, status superseded, supersededByRevisionId set, checksum unchanged, still 200 on download, byte-identical (same sha256 and length). Revision 2 is a genuinely different artifact hashing to its own checksum. Exactly one revision isCurrent. A no-change regeneration manufactures no revision.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.consequence: Of D-028’s five customer requirements — retained, byte-identical, downloadable, marked superseded, linked to successor — only the first two are delivered to the customer. An inspector who filed revision 1 with a client or a regulator cannot see that it exists, cannot tell which revision they filed, and cannot retrieve it. /reports states the opposite as product intent: "Every completed inspection has one report. Finishing an inspection again replaces its report." The server does not replace it.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.alsoOnTheArtifact: The PDF itself carries no revision number and no superseded marking, so a filed report cannot be distinguished from its successor by reading it.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.whyNotRepairedAtSection285: Surfacing revision history is product design — what a customer should see, how a superseded report is labelled, and whether the copy denying versions exist should change. §285 authorised objective repairs, not redesign.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.requiredAction: Product-owner decision on how report revisions are presented, then implement.

canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.consequence: An inspector who walks an area and finds nothing has no way to close the record. The available routes are to record a finding they do not believe in, or to leave the record open — and "we inspected and it was sound" is a result a client may need to be given.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.whyNotChangedAtSection285: Completion policy is the product owner’s; §285 forbids inventing one.
canRunInParallelWithTheBlockers.requiredAction: Decide whether a no-finding inspection may be completed, and what its report says.
